# RustyNES v2.6.14 "Docket"

The submission checklist becomes auditable, and auditing it finds five boxes already true, two ticked on evidence that expired, and one that could never have been ticked honestly.

**The emulation core is unchanged.** No chip crate changes, so AccuracyCoin 141/141 (RAM decoder) and nestest 0-diff hold by construction, and were re-run anyway.

## Why a checklist was the subject

v2.7.0 is the submission: an email to `newcores@misterfpga.org` with a link to the core. `to-dos/mister/contribution-checklist.md` is the list that says whether the repository is ready, and it had 30 boxes, 16 unticked, and **14 of those 16 saying nothing at all about why**.

That ambiguity is the defect. An unticked box with no reason cannot be told apart from three different things: work genuinely outstanding, work blocked on something outside this repository, and **work already done and never ticked**. The audit found the third case five times — the provenance CI job, the SPDX sweep, the firewall statement, the AccuracyCoin vector and the preservation-value case were all true and all unticked — so the list had been reporting the project as further from submission than it is, by a fifth of its own length.

## A box that could never have been ticked honestly

One asked that `docs/provenance.md` state *"that no NES core was ever opened"*.

That same document's § **Do not self-certify** says: *never assert "no third-party code is incorporated" or "licence-clean" as a finished claim ... surface provenance status for human and expert review, and state uncertainty.*

The box could only have been satisfied by writing the one sentence the project's provenance rules exist to prevent. It is not a missing tick; it is a wrong requirement, and only reading every item found it. The firewall half is what was actually being asked for and is ticked; the self-certification half is struck, with the reason recorded in place.

## Two ticked boxes were ticked on evidence that had expired

This is v2.6.9's finding applied to a different document: a stated reason stops being true and nobody re-reads it. Re-measuring the **settled** half of the list, not just the unsettled one, found two.

`RustyNES.sdc` said *"There is exactly one core clock ... so there is no second clock domain to constrain and no false path to cut."* True of v2.6.3's master-clock divider, **false since v2.6.13**, which added `clk_sdram` at 4x and the phase-shifted `clk_sdram_ps`; the shipped timing report names all three core-PLL outputs. The file's behaviour was never wrong — `derive_pll_clocks` picks up all three — only its explanation.

**The alarming reading of that was checked before it was written down.** It looks as though `sys/sys_top.sdc`'s `set_clock_groups -exclusive` might be cutting the `clk_sys` to `clk_sdram` crossing, which would leave ADR 0039's whole safety argument unfalsifiable — an unanalysed crossing cannot be shown safe. It is not: `-exclusive` cuts paths *between* groups, all three outputs match one glob and land in a single group, and v2.6.13's own -24.769 ns measurement of that crossing is only observable because those paths are analysed.

`RustyNES.qsf`'s entry said the device and **all 109** pin assignments come from `sys/sys.tcl`. It supplies 109 — including the 45 SDRAM pins, which is why the SDRAM work needed no pin file of its own — and stops short of the I/O board, so a core must also pick one of two 36-assignment variants. This one sources `sys_analog.tcl`. **145 in total, from two scripts.**

## The naming divergence, measured instead of paraphrased

The checklist said `Distribution_MiSTer` "selects the newest bitstream by the DATE in the filename", which is the wiki's wording. `Main_MiSTer/file_io.cpp` is sharper:

- `get_display_name()` searches the filename for the literal `"_20"`, requires at least six characters after it, then does `*p = 0` — **truncating the display name at that point** — and takes up to fifteen following characters as `datecode`. With no `"_20"`, `datecode` becomes `"------"` and the name is left whole.
- `DirentComp()` compares the truncated names first, and only falls through to `strcasecmp` on the datecodes when they are equal.

`RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.6.13.rbf` contains no `_20`. Three consequences follow, none cosmetic: every released version is a **separate core entry** rather than versions of one; the entry is named `RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.6.13` rather than `RustyNES`; and ordering between them is alphabetic on the version string, so **v2.6.9 sorts after v2.6.13**.

It does **not** affect the Home folder, which comes from `CONF_STR` and is already `RustyNES`, and it has no effect until submission, because nothing harvests `releases/` until the core is accepted. The fix is one line in `scripts/release-rbf.sh` and is **not taken here**: version-naming is a maintainer decision of 2026-08-30 with a stated rationale, and reversing it is not an audit's call.

## The task board had the same defect, one row worse

Four delivered items had never been ticked — v2.6.6's whole rung-6 integration, the SDRAM controller, the published `.rbf` and the Home folder. The hardware row still named **v2.6.7**, seven releases after that slot shipped something else.

The SDRAM row is the interesting one. It said the controller comes **"after a board exists"**, justified by a table asserting it "needs hardware" because "its acceptance is read/write timing against a real part". v2.6.13 did not wait, and accepted it against a **behavioural model written from the same datasheet** — tRCD, tRP, tRAS, tRC, tRFC, tRRD, tMRD and tWR checked, a clock period the part cannot meet refused — then ran the whole console against it at 142 of 142.

That is rung 7's own recorded lesson repeating one row below where it is written: *before recording something as blocked, check the blocker applies to the whole item.* It applied to hardware **acceptance**, not to building the controller.

## A claim v2.6.13 shipped, retracted

Answering a review finding that "a five-mapper core" did not say which five, I wrote that the five were NROM, UxROM, CNROM, AxROM and MMC3, and that **MMC1 was the sixth approved family and not yet implemented**.

Both halves are false. `rtl/cart/cart.sv` decodes mapper 1 at three sites, `mapper1mmc1063` has been a registered gate since rung 7 opened, and NROM landed at v2.6.3 rather than in rung 7's five. The approved six-family scope is **complete**.

It was asserted from memory inside a reply correcting somebody else's reading of the same line. The project's rule is to verify a reviewer's claim before writing the fix; the failure mode is verifying theirs and then not verifying your own. Retracted in the plan with the wrong text preserved, and on the public review thread.

## The gate

`contribution_checklist_audit.rs` asserts a **shape**, not a judgement: a ticked box names the release that settled it, an unticked one carries `BLOCKED`, `DEFERRED`, `DECIDED` or `CONTINGENT`. It deliberately does not rule on whether a verdict is *correct* — it cannot, and a gate that pretends to is the "passes without testing its subject" failure this project keeps finding.

Five mutations: a removed verdict, a removed release tag, every box ticked, and a broken box syntax are all **CAUGHT**; removing the continuation-line folding produces **nine false violations**, which is what proves that rule load-bearing — the verdict markers do not sit on an item's first line.

## What is next, specified rather than named

`cpu_interrupts_v2` sat on the board as "the independent interrupt oracle, now reachable", which is not something anyone can start from. Measured here: **five** independent single-purpose ROMs rather than one combined; **mapper 0**, where the combined ROM is mapper 1, removing MMC1 as a variable; **the oracle passes all five**, so a DUT gate can adjudicate; and they report through `$6000`, so they need `PRG_RAM=1` as the blargg batteries do. Deliberately not started here.

## What no gate here reaches

**No hardware has run this bitstream.** Rung 6 does not close: no DE10-Nano and no SuperStation One are attached to this machine, confirmed by checking rather than assumed. The palette, the video timing constants, the audio absolute level and its band-limiting remain downstream of every gate by construction.
